question: Can Corpuz et al. (2025) support a Bataan-specific Clarias batrachus diet or species assertion for Bangwit?

method.procedure: Reviewed the publisher-hosted full text for bibliographic details, collection sites, methods, sample sizes and dates, stomach-content findings, site-name consistency, data availability, and reuse statements. Compared the study's taxon label with the current Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes entry for Clarias batrachus.
method.scope: Source-quality and taxonomic-identity review only. The paper is not treated as a complete inventory, a current-presence survey, bait guidance, or independent voucher confirmation.

publication.citation: Corpuz, M. N. C., Rojero, R., Ocampo, M. A., & Padilla, E. (2025). Length-weight relationship, condition factor dynamics, and feeding preference of Clarias batrachus (Linnaeus, 1758) from the rivers of Bataan, Luzon Island, Philippines. Aquatic Research, 8(2), 70-78. https://doi.org/10.3153/AR25008.
publication.licenseAssessment: Aquatic Research marks this article Open Access and its journal open-access statement specifies CC BY 4.0. The extracted PDF text shows © 2025 The Author(s), but no article-specific license line was located. Attribute the article if citing; do not copy figures, maps, tables, or photographs because this review does not establish separate item-level image rights or app reuse approval.

reportedSampling.localityConflict: The methods and Figure 1 caption give different Bagac locality names (Silahis-Pag-asa versus Parang). Without a station crosswalk or author clarification, retain both as source-reported labels and do not use either as precise point or reach geometry.
reportedSampling.dietMethod: Stomach contents from all 60 fish were examined; prey items were sorted and identified to the lowest possible taxonomic level under a simple microscope. The paper reports count, frequency, weight, volume, and diet-index summaries.
reportedSampling.voucherEvidence: No museum voucher number, specimen-level identifier, sequence accession, or diagnostic taxonomic documentation linking the Bataan samples was found in the reviewed article.

Bagac.sourceHighlightedPrey: Fish; the paper names Glossogobius giuris and reports fish as the leading category by number and frequency in Bagac.
Bagac.interpretation: Sample-specific gut-content observation from the sampled Bagac fish, conditional on the source's unresolved species identification and locality reporting.

Orani.sourceHighlightedPrey: Insects, reported as the leading category in the Orani sample.
Orani.interpretation: Sample-specific gut-content observation from the sampled Orani fish, conditional on the source's unresolved species identification.

reportedDietFindings.limits: The two small site samples do not establish a universal diet, seasonal diet, current population status, fish occurrence outside the study's own capture event, or bait effectiveness. Keep natural diet evidence distinct from bait suggestions.

taxonomicCrosscheck.reference: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes, Clarias batrachus entry, current status valid; distribution note says the species is definitely known only from river drainages in Java and introduced elsewhere, citing Ng & Kottelat (2008).
taxonomicCrosscheck.assessment: The Bataan paper's species label is in tension with the Catalog's restricted native-range statement. The Catalog note is a reason to require specimen-level verification; it is not proof that the Bataan specimens are absent, misidentified, or any particular alternative species.
taxonomicCrosscheck.identityDecision: Held pending voucher, diagnostic, or sequence crosswalk. Do not silently rename or project the reported taxon.

dataAvailability.sourceStatement: The article states that study data will be made available on request.
dataAvailability.decision: No author data request was sent as part of this source review.

acceptedForResearchOnly: A 2025 source-reported gut-content study sampled 30 fish at each of two Bataan river systems in August-November 2023.
The paper reports fish prey as prominent in Bagac and insects as prominent in Orani, with additional prey categories at both sites.
The methods and figure caption disagree on the Bagac locality name.
The source taxon label remains unresolved against the Catalog of Fishes distribution note because no linked voucher or accession was located.
evidenceDisposition.decision: Keep as an attributed, research-only local natural-diet lead. Do not publish a species identity, occurrence, diet card, bait recommendation, locality geometry, or image from this source until taxon identity, locality, and intended reuse are resolved.

nextActions: If the finding is needed for the public diet feature, seek a specimen-level voucher, diagnostic account, or sequence crosswalk from the authors or an accessible collection; do not infer identity from the article title.
Resolve the Bagac Silahis-Pag-asa versus Parang figure-caption conflict before using any fine-scale locality.
Keep the source's dietary findings separate from bait recommendations and from broader species or current-presence claims.
Keep Central Luzon and Luzon marked incomplete until their waterbody, taxon, source, and locality evidence are independently reconciled.

sources.supports: Full-text citation, sampling design, source-reported taxon and localities, locality-caption conflict, sample counts, collection period, and gut-content categories and site-level differences.
Publisher article metadata, DOI, publication date, and Open Access label.
Journal open-access statement specifying CC BY 4.0 for its open-access articles.
Current status of Clarias batrachus and the Catalog's Java-only definitely-known range note with introduced-elsewhere qualifier.
